title: What is philosophy?
examples: What is the difference between philosophy and science?
Can you give me an example of a big question in philosophy?
How do I start thinking like a philosopher?

explain.say: Philosophy is really about asking big questions.
When we ask why, we start thinking deeply.

items: Question: Why is the sky blue?

explain.say: Arguments help us explore these big ideas clearly.
Ethics asks about what is right and what is wrong.
Logic is the study of good and bad thinking.
Metaphysics asks about the nature of reality itself.

faq.q: What is the difference between philosophy and science?
faq.a: Science uses experiments to test ideas about the physical world. Philosophy uses reason and arguments to explore big questions that science might not answer.

faq.q: Do I need to memorize philosophers to be good at philosophy?
faq.a: No, philosophy is more about learning how to think clearly. It is about the process of questioning, not just knowing names.
asks: Is it hard to study philosophy?
Do I need to read all the big books?

faq.q: How do I know if my argument is strong?
faq.a: You check if your premises actually support your conclusion. A strong argument has premises that are true and that connect logically.
asks: How do I spot a weak argument?

faq.q: Is ethics just about following rules?
faq.a: No, ethics looks at the reasons behind rules. It asks if a rule is always right, even if it is easy to follow.
asks: Is ethics the same as law?
Do I have to follow what ethics says?

faq.a: Metaphysics studies what is fundamentally real. It asks questions like, does time really pass, or is it just a concept?

facts: Philosophy is the love of wisdom.
Ethics guides our decisions about right and wrong actions.
Logic provides tools for analyzing arguments.
Metaphysics explores the basic nature of reality.

quiz.say: If you ask, 'What is the meaning of life?', which branch are you exploring?
quiz.why: This question asks about the fundamental nature of existence, which is the study of metaphysics.

wrong.0: Ethics focuses on whether the meaning of life is good or bad for people.
wrong.1: Logic would ask if the statement 'the meaning of life is X' can even be proven.
wrong.2: Science looks for physical evidence, but 'meaning' is not a physical thing.

quiz.say: Which tool helps you check if your reasons lead to a true conclusion?
quiz.why: Logic is the formal study of reasoning, helping you build sound arguments.

wrong.1: Metaphysics asks what is real, not how to connect ideas correctly.
wrong.2: Ethics tells you if a conclusion is morally right, not if it is logically sound.
wrong.3: Observation is just noticing something; logic is the skill of connecting those notices.

quiz.say: When deciding if lying is ever okay, you are mainly using ideas from:
quiz.why: Ethics is the branch that examines moral principles and right conduct.

wrong.0: Metaphysics would ask if the concept of 'truth' itself exists outside of our minds.
wrong.1: Logic would check if 'lying is okay' follows from any initial rules you set.
wrong.2: Science can tell you the consequences of lying, but not if it is morally right.
